events.title: Francis Drake Is Knighted Aboard the Golden Hind
events.description: Queen Elizabeth I knighted the English sea captain Francis Drake. He had just returned from a voyage around the world that brought home vast Spanish treasure.
events.significance: The knighthood honored Drake's circumnavigation of the globe and showed England's growing ambition as a naval power. It also signaled its willingness to challenge Spain at sea.

events.title: William Henry Harrison Dies in Office
events.description: President William Henry Harrison died of illness just 31 days after taking office. He was the first U.S. president to die while serving.
events.significance: Harrison's death had no clear precedent. It forced the young republic to settle how power passes to a vice president, and John Tyler set the model by assuming the full presidency.

events.title: NATO Treaty Signed in Washington
events.description: Twelve nations signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, D.C. The treaty created the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance built on mutual defense.
events.significance: NATO became the cornerstone of Western security during the Cold War. It remains one of the world's most influential military alliances.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Is Assassinated
events.description: The civil rights leader Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was shot and killed in Memphis, Tennessee. He was there to support striking sanitation workers.
events.significance: His death shocked the United States and set off grief and unrest across the country. It also strengthened the push for civil rights and fair housing legislation, and his legacy still shapes the fight for equality.
